title: Add a level with its own floor plan view and a structural grid
task: Create a Level with Level.Create, then the floor plan it does not get automatically: find the FloorPlan ViewFamilyType and call ViewPlan.Create(doc, viewTypeId, levelId); look a plan up by ViewPlan.GenLevel; add a Grid with Grid.Create from a Line. A GenLevel lookup on a script-created level finds nothing until the plan exists.

pitfalls.symptom: NewRoomTag or NewDimension throws an ArgumentNullException deep inside Revit after creating a level with Level.Create.
pitfalls.cause: The view argument was null: the plan lookup by ViewPlan.GenLevel found nothing because Level.Create does not create a floor plan view. The calls do not require the view to look at the element's level.
pitfalls.fix: Create the plan with ViewPlan.Create(doc, floorPlanViewFamilyTypeId, level.Id) (step 4) and pass it, or pass any existing non-template plan.

pitfalls.symptom: Setting Level.Name throws: the name is already in use.
pitfalls.fix: Check existing names first or use a distinct suffix.

pitfalls.symptom: Filtering plans by GenLevel throws a NullReferenceException.
pitfalls.cause: Some ViewPlan elements (templates, plans without a level) have a null GenLevel.
pitfalls.fix: Skip IsTemplate views and null GenLevel before comparing ids (step 5).

provenance.ref: revit/test-harness/harness_test.go TestCreateLevel; phase_b_test.go CreateRoomAndTagIt (the plan-view finding); phase_c_test.go CreateGrid
